_comment: The community's roster: who has an account on the record server. Copy this to
community.json and edit. Names only — no passwords appear in this file, and none
should ever be added to it. bootstrap.py generates a strong password for each
account, sends it to the server once, and writes it to ~/.ndex/symposium.env with
owner-only permissions. Nothing secret lives in the repository, and nobody has to
type or paste a password anywhere.
JSON rather than TOML because this toolchain is standard-library-only on Python
3.9, where tomllib does not exist. A hand-rolled parser for a config format is a
new way to be silently wrong about who is in a community.
The admin account runs the gate. It is the only account that can accept an
Artifact into the record, and every member grants it READ on a submission as the
act of submitting. Members are the accounts that publish. A Member is a person, a
laboratory, or an agent — the specification does not say which, and neither does
Adding a member later: add the name here and run bootstrap.py again. It is
